newsitem.title: BRAZIL: France's Chirac says keep up momentum of Brazil visit.
newsitem.headline: France's Chirac says keep up momentum of Brazil visit.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac on Thursday tried to lay to rest an old Brazilian complaint, denying that Gen. Charles de Gaulle ever said in a famous gibe: "Brazil is not a serious country."

"De Gaulle never said that. This was a fabrication," Chirac said as he ended his state visit in Brazil's economic powerhouse of Sao Paulo, a trip hailed as a major step toward boosting bilateral economic exchanges.
"I found Brazil to be an extraordinarily serious country ... but without losing its enthusiasm and charm, and that is among its main assets," he told a news conference.

Throughout his 48-hour visit to Brasilia, Rio and Sao Paulo, Chirac praised the restoration of Brazil's democracy and economy, calling the country one of the great economic and political powers of the 21st century and saying it had major trade prospects with the European Union and France.

He said France had been "too absent from the region for too long" and he hoped his visit would revive hopes for a strong partnership raised, but unfulfilled, by de Gaulle's visit to Latin America more than three decades ago.
"I hope we have created momentum, and I am determined that it will not lag," he said.

Earlier, addressing hundreds of Brazilian and French businessmen at the powerful Brazilian Industries Federation headquarters, he urged them to transform the two governments' will to boost exchanges into increased trade.
"Work together more, you who are on both sides of the Atlantic building tomorrow's growth and prosperity," he said.
Chirac was to fly to Uruguay on the second stage of a week-long tour to the four countries of the South American Mercosur customs union, which also includes Argentina and Paraguay, and to Bolivia.
Chirac dismissed reports that his foray into the traditional zone of U.S. influence to boost the role of France and its EU partners could anger Washington.

"Brazil belongs to America through geography, to Europe through culture, to the world through its interests ... Brazil cannot ignore the EU. The EU is Brazil's and Mercosur's biggest partner. This is a fact," he said.
Slow to react to the emergence of Mercosur, Paris has fallen badly behind some of its EU partners in exchanges with the group, although French trade and investment zoomed last year.
French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette told Reuters Chirac's visit had been "a total and unblemished success."

Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso told the businessmen Paris and Brasilia had restored mutual trust but he repeated a longstanding call for the EU to lower trade barriers to farm products from Mercosur.
Chirac said Mercosur was exporting many more farm products than it was importing from the EU and trade problems were due to poor organisation of the world food production and markets.

Chirac, aware of the Latin American passion for soccer, invited former French soccer captain Michel Platini to join him on his tour and said his "soccer diplomacy" worked wonders when both dined with soccer legend Pele in Rio on Wednesday.
"All reporters mobbed Platini and ignored me. It allowed me to have a quiet moment," he said.
